chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabī' al-Shami who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked, with the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate, and by Him we seek help,
"And to God belongs the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find a way to it."

He said, 'What do the people say?' I said to him, 'The provisions and the mount.' He said, 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about this and said, 'People would perish if so, for if everyone who has provisions and a mount sufficient to feed his family and make him independent of people goes to them and deprives them of it, they would indeed perish.' It was said to him, 'Then what is the way?' He said, 'Ease in wealth, if he performs pilgrimage with part of it and keeps part for the food of his family. Has not God made zakat obligatory, and He did not make it obligatory except upon one who possesses two hundred dirhams?'

key_terms.مِائَتَيْ دِرْهَمٍ: Two hundred dirhams (a standard measure of wealth)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'ability' (istita'ah) for the obligation of Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the simplistic view that 'ability' merely means possessing food and a mount, arguing that such a standard would cause universal ruin by stripping families of their livelihood. He defines istita'ah as financial ease (sa'ah) where one retains sufficient surplus for family sustenance after Hajj expenses, drawing a parallel to the nisab threshold for zakat to ensure the obligation does not impose undue hardship.
